correctness.rationale: The quotient is exactly the reciprocal norm of a convex combination of a unit Birkhoff--James orthogonal pair. Support-functional orthogonality and dihedral symmetry reduce every such chord to three triangles: one from an edge-interior base point and two from a vertex base point. On each triangle a unit-dual facet functional or convex combination gives a rigorous lower bound; the common smallest bound is \((7+5\sqrt3)/26\). An explicit chord point has exactly that norm, so the reciprocal is \(5\sqrt3-7\). The finalized bundled checker verifies all algebraic identities and named facet incidences from the packaged path.
risks: The geometric reduction is specific to the twelve-facet polygon and does not automatically extend to other regular polygons.
Finite symbolic checks verify the named certificates; the completeness of the three-region reduction is supplied analytically in the proof, not inferred from sampling.

value.rationale: The rectangular constant is a classical quantitative Hilbert/non-squareness invariant, and the modern primary source treats exact two-dimensional polygonal cases as structurally informative. The regular dodecagon is the next canonical quarter-turn-symmetric regular polygon beyond the already-computed square and octagonal benchmarks, but its orthogonality geometry is qualitatively richer: both edge and vertex normal cones are active. The finding gives an exact global chord-depth theorem with three sharp polyhedral certificates, not merely a numerical evaluation. That decomposition is reusable for rectangular constants of other polygonal norms.
risks: The result is a canonical exact benchmark rather than a complete all-regular-polygon classification.
